newsitem.title: DUBAI: PRESS DIGEST - United Arab Emirates - April 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - United Arab Emirates - April 28.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the United Arab Emirates press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Dubai Crown Prince and UAE Defence Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid al-Maktoum instructed Dubai authorities to curb the practice of share purchases using other people's names.

- Emaar Properties raised the share quota for nationals. The quota for UAE nationals and 100 percent nationally owned companies in Emaar's recent public offer has been raised to 657 million dirhams from 297 million dirhams.
- A study said the illiteracy rate among women in the UAE had dropped to 11.3 percent in 1995 from 77.6 percent in 1980.
- The UAE could be the first country in the Middle East to become a full-fledged manufacturer of medium-to-large naval vessels, European defence sources said.
- The secretary general of Lebanon's Hezbollah is visting Iran and will hold talks with officials on the situation in Lebanon.
- Emirates said it was seeking to increase the airline's share of traffic from destinations in northeast Asia.

- The UAE emirate of Sharjah, where alcohol is prohibited, has banned the sale of 'non-alcoholic' malt beer in all of its food outlets following the discovery of traces of alcohol in various brands of the product, a municipality official said.
- Oman's commerce minister travelled to Geneva on Sunday to discuss his country's application for membership in the World Trade Organsiation.
